title: Object-Oriented Design Principles
learning_outcomes: Explain what object-oriented design principles contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: single responsibility.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. In this lesson, focus on single responsibility; then compare it with open/closed principle. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use object-oriented design principles when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Advanced object design is about collaboration and stable contracts. Interfaces, composition, dependency injection, namespaces, and autoloading help change or test parts independently. For object-oriented design principles, begin with single responsibility. Also distinguish open/closed principle; liskov substitution; interface segregation. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Use the smallest representative example, make expected behavior explicit, and test normal plus boundary inputs.

content_blocks.title: Walk through one example
content_blocks.text: Read the example for object-oriented design principles from top to bottom. Start by identifying single responsibility, write down the relevant variable values or control-flow choice, and predict the expected output before running it. Then change one input or condition, check a boundary case, and explain why the result changed.

content.task: Create a second small example for object-oriented design principles that demonstrates "single responsibility". Before running it, write down the expected result and one boundary case.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example includes a clear use of single responsibility.
The learner can explain its input, rule, and observable output.
At least one edge case is tested or documented.
hints: Start with the most direct listed subtopic and a single input.
Keep the example small enough that you can predict the output manually.
Test one normal case and one empty, invalid, or boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
